piece_type: DTC TV ad (US-ANK-250065-v1) and DTC podcast “Is the FDA BLOCKING Life Saving Cancer Treatments?” (The Sean Spicer Show, Jan 19, 2026) featuring company executive

cases.claim: “...There's an ability to actually create a cancer vaccine so that we can treat the tumor, and it doesn't come back.” | “[IL-15]...the most important molecule that could cure cancer…nobody could figure out how to get IL-15 into your body with a single jab, and that is Anktiva.” | “ANKTIVA BioShield” | “...this little vial that you inject subcutaneously that really is on the path to curing the cancer.” | “Cancer Therapeutic Vaccine (BioShield).”
cases.context: PI QUILT-3.032 single-arm (n=77, with BCG): CR 62%; of responders 58% DoR ≥12 mo, 40% ≥24 mo. Single-agent Cohort C stopped for futility. DFS uninterpretable (single-arm). MoA: IL-15 receptor agonist, not a vaccine. Bad Ad complaints.
cases.rationale: Suggests long-term cancer-free status/cure for all patients, single-agent effect, and vaccine/preventive properties — not demonstrated; 'vaccine' is false.
cases.check: Rule: lexicon flag 'cure', 'doesn't come back', 'vaccine', 'prevent' vs PI; flag single-agent framing when PI indication is combination.

cases.claim: “It’s approved for bladder cancer, but it actually can treat all cancers.” | “This thing called checkpoint inhibitors…It fails. The only thing that can rescue it is Anktiva…If you have lung cancer, ...” | “We have the therapy to prevent cancer if you were exposed to radiation and that’s Anktiva.” | “single jab” | “little vial that you inject subcutaneously” | [Visual] TV ad shows vial removed from carton, HCP preparing a dose, patients injected in the arm
cases.context: PI: intravesical use only; not for SC/IV/IM. Approved only for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS in combination with BCG.
cases.rationale: Evidence of intended new uses (all cancers, lung cancer, prevention, injectable routes) lacking adequate directions for use.
cases.check: Rule: flag any disease, population, or route of administration not in PI Indications / D&A (e.g., 'subcutaneous' for an intravesical product).

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
cases.claim: [Format] TV ad risk information appears only after VO “To learn more, visit immunitybio.com” and the screen fades to black, with no signal that risk follows
cases.context: Benefit visuals: vials, patients receiving treatment, “treat the tumor”, “cancer free”.
cases.rationale: Risk not comparable in prominence to benefits; minimizes risks.
cases.check: Rule: flag risk content placed after closing cues (fade to black, URL sign-off); require pre-signal.

cases.claim: “Think 53+ months duration of response.” | “If you have CIS and papillary, I can treat you. It’s approved.” | [Omission] podcast includes no risk information
cases.context: Podcast displays consumer website landing page.
cases.rationale: Benefit claims with no risk information.
cases.check: Rule: executive podcasts/interviews naming product with benefit claims require risk information.

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.claim: [Omission] TV ad and podcast do not specify use in combination with BCG for adults with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS with or without papillary tumors; full indication shown only after fade to black
cases.context: Podcast: “for CIS with or without papillary”.
cases.check: Rule: indication must include combination partner and BCG-unresponsive qualifier, before closing cues.

cases.cat: Failure to submit at first use (Form FDA 2253)
cases.claim: [Process] podcast not submitted under Form FDA 2253 at initial publication
cases.context: Executive podcast appearance hosted on company website.
cases.check: Process rule: executive media appearances require 2253.
